privacy.forget.title: DEINE DATEN LÖSCHEN
privacy.forget.body:
Ich lösche deine Verknüpfungen, die privaten Hinweise, deine Aktivität, die laufende Saison, die Titel auf deinen Namen in den Clans, in denen ich ein Tag von dir habe, die Notiz der Anführer und die Nachrichten in der Warteschlange.

Schon archivierte Kriege bleiben: das sind Spieldaten am Tag und sie laufen nach 100 Kriegen aus. Die Clan-Zeile setzt die Clash-API bei jeder Runde neu, solange du im Clan bist: deshalb nehme ich dich auch aus den öffentlichen Ranglisten und lasse dich draußen. Ein Titel aus einem Clan, den du verlassen hast, bleibt ebenfalls: in der Ruhmeshalle steht nur der Name des Siegers, und ohne ein Tag von dir dort kann ich dich von einem Namensvetter nicht unterscheiden.
privacy.forget.stays: Der Bot, den du erstellt hast, bleibt deiner: der Besitz innerhalb von Telegram wandert hier nicht weg. Du verwaltest ihn über /mybots in der ClanBoard-Konsole.
privacy.forget.done: Gelöscht: {links} Verknüpfungen, {activity} Aktivitätsblätter, {season} Saisoneinträge, {titles} Titel, {notes} Notizen.

web.privacy.title: Privacy
web.privacy.intro: In plain words and without lawyer language: this is everything ClanBoard knows about you, where it keeps it and for how long.
web.privacy.collect.title: What we collect
web.privacy.collect.body: The public game data read from the official Clash of Clans API: clan, roster, wars. The Telegram id and the name of whoever links a village or manages a clan. The clan settings and the texts written by the managers. The day the terms were accepted. Nothing else: no contacts, no location, no phone number.
web.privacy.where.title: Where it lives
web.privacy.where.body: On a single server in Europe. The database is encrypted row by row; the backups are encrypted with the same key and only the last three are kept, the others delete themselves at every nightly backup.
web.privacy.keep.title: How long it stays
web.privacy.keep.body: The history keeps the last {wars} wars per clan, and the same cap holds for the manager log, the former members and the CWL seasons. A clan that stops showing up is deleted after {days} days. News and temporary notes have an expiry and go away on their own.
web.privacy.rights.title: Your rights
web.privacy.rights.body: From the app, «My data» hands you everything about you and «Forget me» deletes it: link, news, seat, warnings and notes. The clan leader can remove the bot from the group and close everything.
web.privacy.never.title: What we never do
web.privacy.never.body: We sell nothing and hand nothing over to anyone. No tracking, no profiling cookies, no ads, no third party beyond Telegram, the Clash of Clans API and Cloudflare carrying the pages.
web.privacy.contact.title: If something looks wrong
web.privacy.contact.body: Tell us before anything else: the rules for reporting are here.
web.privacy.license: The code is free, AGPL-3.0 licence: read it, check it, run it yourself.
web.terms.title: Terms
web.terms.intro: ClanBoard is free and open. Using it means accepting these few lines.
web.terms.who.title: Who can use it
web.terms.who.body: You need a Telegram account, with the minimum age Telegram asks for, and to manage a clan a village linked with the game token. One bot per clan, one clan per group.
web.terms.rules.title: What you must not do
web.terms.rules.body: No spam, scams, harassment or illegal content in the texts the bot publishes; no attempts to get around the limits or to enter where you should not; no use of the game data outside the Supercell terms.
web.terms.service.title: The service as it is
web.terms.service.body: It is free and without warranty: it can stop, get a count wrong or skip a round, and the game data is worth what the official API is worth. There is nothing to pay and nothing to unlock.
web.terms.stop.title: When it stops
web.terms.stop.body: A bot used for harassment or scams is suspended and the clan can be removed. On the other side, the clan leader stops whenever they want: remove the bot from the group and that is the end of it.
web.terms.license: The code is under the AGPL-3.0 licence: you can read it, change it and run it yourself, under the same conditions.
